value_proposition: Provides superconducting quantum processors and supporting technology for research and innovation, emphasizing rapid access through a 9-qubit Novera QPU advertised as ready to ship.
target_customers: Organizations conducting quantum hardware and algorithm R&D
Developers exploring quantum optimization and other applications
hardware_architecture: Superconducting quantum hardware cooled by a dilution refrigerator. The supplied R&D material also describes fixed-frequency transmons with a floating tunable coupler for CZ gates, but it does not establish that this exact architecture is used in every commercial system.
current_systems: Novera — 9-qubit QPU advertised as ready to ship and available to order
Cepheus-1-108Q — listed under 'Rigetti Right Now' with 107 qubits and a deployment date of 04.07.26
physical_qubit_scale: Currently advertised systems span 9 qubits for Novera and 107 reported qubits for Cepheus-1-108Q, despite the latter's 108Q model name.
one_qubit_fidelity: Cepheus-1-108Q: 99.85% median fidelity per single-qubit gate operation.
two_qubit_fidelity: Cepheus-1-108Q: 98.79% median fidelity per two-qubit CZ operation.
coherence: Cepheus-1-108Q: median T1 lifetime of 27 µs and median T2 lifetime of 11 µs.
error_correction_strategy: Rigetti reports demonstrating low-latency feedback using a scalable FPGA decoder integrated into the control system of a superconducting quantum processor. The source does not identify the error-correcting code, logical error rate, code distance, or demonstrated logical-qubit count.
fault_tolerance_strategy: The research direction is to support scalable, low-latency real-time decoding and maintain a fast logical clock rate while advancing toward a universal fault-tolerant logical gate set. A universal fault-tolerant gate set is described as a future objective, not a demonstrated capability.
roadmap: Research direction: advance toward demonstrating a universal fault-tolerant logical gate set
Develop scalable, low-latency real-time decoding to avoid excessive logical-computation slowdown
Continue R&D on fast, high-fidelity CZ gates, residual-ZZ cancellation, and integrated on-chip thermometry
access_methods: Direct ordering of the Novera QPU
QCS sign-in, documentation, and support links are provided, although the supplied material does not define the service or confirm cloud hardware availability
commercial_deployments: Cepheus-1-108Q is labeled 'Deployed' with the date 04.07.26, but no customer, location, use case, or access terms are disclosed
strengths: A 9-qubit QPU is advertised as immediately orderable and ready to ship, offering a direct hardware-access proposition
The homepage reports a deployed 107-qubit processor with disclosed median coherence and gate-fidelity metrics
Integrated hardware and software branding spans QPUs, QCS, programming tools, compiler technology, and simulation
R&D addresses practical fault-tolerance infrastructure, including FPGA-based low-latency decoding
R&D also targets component-level issues such as local chip thermometry, CZ-gate performance, and residual-ZZ cancellation
weaknesses: No demonstrated logical-qubit count or logical error-rate improvement is disclosed
The reported 98.79% median two-qubit fidelity is materially below the reported 99.85% single-qubit fidelity, leaving two-qubit errors as an important limitation
Median T2 of 11 µs is relatively short in absolute terms, while no gate-duration data is provided to assess the available operation budget
No connectivity topology, measurement fidelity, system uptime, throughput, calibration stability, or variability data is supplied
The source does not connect the error-correction demonstration to a protected logical qubit or fault-tolerant logical operation
Commercial deployment evidence is limited to a single unlabeled 'Deployed' entry without customer or workload details
competitive_differentiators: Direct shipment proposition for the 9-qubit Novera QPU
Combination of a small orderable QPU and a reported 107-qubit deployed processor
Vertically integrated portfolio covering superconducting hardware, control-system R&D, programming tools, compilation, simulation, and service/support links
Research emphasis on low-latency FPGA decoding integrated with the quantum control system
technical_risks: The supplied evidence does not demonstrate useful logical computation, logical error suppression, or a fault-tolerant logical gate
Scaling low-latency decoding from a feedback demonstration to sustained fault-tolerant computation may introduce control, synchronization, and decoder-throughput challenges
A 98.79% median CZ fidelity may require substantial further improvement and/or error-correction overhead for fault-tolerant operation
The combination of an 11 µs median T2 and undisclosed gate speeds makes circuit-depth and error-correction-cycle feasibility difficult to assess
The source does not disclose connectivity, fabrication yield, qubit uniformity, crosstalk, leakage, measurement performance, or stability at the 107-qubit scale
R&D results involving floating tunable couplers and Dayem-bridge thermometry may require additional engineering before broad product integration
commercialization_risks: The source provides no customer identities, deployment use cases, pricing, delivery lead times, warranties, or support terms
Shipping a QPU may still require substantial cryogenic, control, facilities, and integration infrastructure, none of which is clarified
QCS links are present, but cloud availability, service levels, capacity, and pricing are not established by the supplied material
The commercial value of the 107-qubit system cannot be evaluated from qubit count alone because logical performance, application benchmarks, and reliability data are absent
The chronology is difficult to validate from the supplied page because it contains deployment and publication dates in 2026, and the date format is not explained
marketing_message: “Quantum. Quick.” Rigetti presents Novera as a 9-qubit QPU ready to ship today, promising unusually direct access to quantum technology for advanced research.
messaging_gaps: The claim of 'unprecedented access' is not supported with comparative access, pricing, queue-time, or delivery data
The ready-to-ship message does not explain whether a complete operating system, cryogenic infrastructure, installation, or only the QPU is included
The homepage does not clearly distinguish product capabilities from experimental R&D results
The significance of the discrepancy between the Cepheus-1-108Q name and its reported 107 qubits is not explained
No application-level performance or logical-computation result is provided to contextualize physical-qubit count and gate fidelity
The QCS access model and the identities of technology or distribution partners are not explained
data_gaps: Demonstrated logical-qubit count and logical fidelity
Logical error rates, code distance, error-correction code, break-even results, and repeated-cycle performance
Gate durations, measurement duration, reset time, and full error-correction cycle time
Readout fidelity, reset fidelity, leakage, crosstalk, and simultaneous-gate performance
Uptime, calibration frequency, reliability, throughput, and benchmark results
Metric distributions and uncertainty beyond reported medians
Exact Novera fidelities, coherence, connectivity, and control specifications
Confirmation of cloud access and on-premises installation options
Pricing, shipping scope, installation requirements, and delivery terms
Customer names, deployment locations, workloads, and commercial outcomes
Manufacturing process, fabrication partners, yield, packaging, and scale-up strategy
Named technology partners and distribution channels
Formal roadmap dates and quantitative milestones
Clarification of the 2026 dates and the 107-qubit count for the Cepheus-1-108Q system
